extracted.intended_audience: newspaper readers, policymakers, and members of Congress
extracted.subtask_short: unifying army and navy into one department
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of criteria and specifications from President Truman’s message recommending consolidation of the War and Navy departments into a single Department of National Defense and related postwar defense recommendations. The page lists principal arguments for unification and specific organizational details the President proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated strategic plans, programs and budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: We should have integrated strategic plans, programs, and budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed by the President as the first of nine main arguments for combining the War and Navy departments to enable coherent long-range strategic planning and budgeting across land, sea, and air forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified control of supply and service functions (economies)
rubrics_metrics.description: We should realize the economies that can be achieved through unified control of supply and service functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argued to produce economies in supply and other functions by removing duplication between departments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational structure to foster civilian-military coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: We should adopt the organizational structure best suited to fostering co-ordination between the military and the remainder of the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President asserts a single department would better coordinate military activities with civilian branches of government and policy objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen civilian control of the military
rubrics_metrics.description: We should provide the strongest means for civilian control of the military.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President recommends a civilian head of the department, civilian under-secretary and assistant secretaries, and other checks (subject to President, Congress and the will of the people) to avoid militarism; emphasized as essential to democracy and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parity for air power
rubrics_metrics.description: We should organize to provide parity for air power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated that parity for air power has been developed and its responsibilities equal those of land and sea; 'Parity for air power can be achieved in one department or in three, but not in two'—used to argue for single department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified system of training for combined operations
rubrics_metrics.description: We should establish the most advantageous framework for a unified system of training for combined operations of land, sea and air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues unified training will prepare forces to operate together effectively in joint operations; cited as needed because of differences in doctrine, training and procedures among services experienced in WWII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic allocation of limited resources for scientific research
rubrics_metrics.description: We should allocate systematically our limited resources for scientific research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President argues unified management would better prioritize and allocate scarce resources for defense-related scientific research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of command in outlying bases
rubrics_metrics.description: We should have unity of command in outlying bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President specified that all military authority at each base should come from a single authority in Washington and that unified command in outlying bases would reduce coordination problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent and equitable personnel policies
rubrics_metrics.description: We should have consistent and equitable personnel policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites differing Army and Navy policies on promotions, discharges, awards, and point allowances as problematic; unification would end such differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single department of national defense
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be a single department of national defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified as the primary structural change: combining the War and Navy departments into one department as the foundation for the other proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civilian head with civilian under-secretary and assistant secretaries
rubrics_metrics.description: The head of this department should be a civilian. Under him there should be a civilian under-secretary and several civilian assistant secretaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasized to ensure civilian control and avoid militarism; these civilian officials would be responsible and accountable to President and Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three co-ordinated branches (land, naval, air) each under assistant secretary
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be three co-ordinated branches of the department: one for the land forces, one for the naval forces, and one for the air forces, each under an assistant secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains distinct branch identities while placing them within a single department structure for coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible assignment of under-secretary and assistant secretaries
rubrics_metrics.description: The under-secretary and the remaining assistant secretaries should be available for assignment to whatever duties the President and the secretary may determine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides administrative flexibility so civilian leadership can be reassigned to meet evolving needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to establish central coordinating and service organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The President and the secretary should be provided with ample authority to establish central co-ordinating and service organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives executive authority to create centralized bureaus for strategic planning, budgeting, supply and service functions to realize economies and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chief of staff plus commanders for each branch
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be a chief of staff. There should also be a commander for each of the three component branches—Army, Navy and Air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a central military chief of staff for overall coordination while retaining commanders responsible for each branch's operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory body of chief of staff and branch commanders; rotation of chief
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief of staff and commanders of the three co-ordinate branches should together constitute an advisory body to the secretary and to the President. It would be wise if the post of chief of staff were rotated among the several services, whenever practicable and advisable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory council intended to balance influence among services and reduce domination by any one service; rotation of chief of staff recommended as an additional safeguard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal military training (separate but related recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Universal military training should be instituted at the earliest possible moment to provide a reserve upon which we can draw.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President treats universal training as 'another essential step—along with unification' for comprehensive and continuous national security; argued necessary because demobilization reduces reliance on WWII veterans.
